instruction: I accidentally closed the slides pane. Can you show it again so I can navigate between slides?

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(5); pyautogui.press('esc'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('f10'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('right', presses=2, interval=0.1); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('down', presses=11, interval=0.1); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.explanation: Task requires restoring the slides pane for navigation. The evaluator verifies that 'Slides View' is present in the accessibility tree.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: checks if 'Slides View' panel is present and visible in the accessibility tree
Metric uses comprehensive search strategy: iterates all elements without type filtering, checks both 'name' attribute and text content for 'Slides View'
Proper visibility verification: checks 'showing' and 'visible' attributes to ensure panel is actually displayed, not just present in DOM
Good error handling: wraps XML parsing in try-except with logging for debugging
Complete coverage: if 'Slides View' panel is visible, the user can navigate between slides as requested in instruction
Handles edge cases well: accepts elements without showing/visible attributes (common in LibreOffice), supports both exact and partial name matches
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Could add more detailed logging to distinguish between 'panel not found' vs 'panel found but not visible' for better debugging
Minor: Could validate that the panel element has a reasonable role attribute (e.g., 'panel', 'scroll pane') though this may not be necessary given LibreOffice's accessibility tree structure
